t: Latest Time by Replacing Hidden Digits
o:
We want the numerically largest valid clock time between 00:00 and 23:59 whose visible digits agree with the pattern `hh:mm`; question marks are wildcards we may fill freely. Greedy filling works digit by digit, but the two hour digits interact: the tens digit wants to be 2, yet that forces units ≤ 3, so if the units digit is pinned above 3 (say 7) the tens must fall back to 1. Minute digits are independent — tens caps at 5, units at 9.

Trace the samples: "2?:?0" keeps tens 2, fills units with 3 and minute tens with 5 giving 23:50. "0?:3?" fills hour units with 9 and minute units with 9 giving 09:39. "1?:22" has units fixed at 2 ≤ 3 so the hidden tens goes as high as allowed, 19:22.

There are only five characters and at most 1440 candidate times, so even a full scan over the clock face is trivially cheap. That makes two clean strategies viable: an exhaustive scan from 23:59 downward (immune to case analysis bugs) and a constant-time greedy that resolves the hour digits jointly.
k: A naive per-digit greedy breaks: choosing 2 for the hour tens is only safe when the units digit can end up ≤ 3.
Treat the two hour digits jointly; minutes are independent (tens ≤ 5, units ≤ 9).
Only 1440 times exist, so scanning candidates from 23:59 downward is a legitimate brute-force alternative.

a.n: Approach 1: Brute Force Over All Times
a.i: Iterate hours from 23 down to 0 and minutes from 59 down to 0, format hh:mm, and accept the first candidate that matches every non-wildcard character. Correct by construction, and it doubles as a validator for the smarter solution.
s: Loop h from 23 down to 0 and m from 59 down to 0.
Format the candidate as two digits, colon, two digits.
If every position matches the pattern (? acts as wildcard), return it.
a.t: O(1440 · 5) — at most every clock face, five comparisons each.
a.sp: O(1) besides the formatted candidate string.

a.n: Approach 2: Joint Greedy on the Hour Digits
a.i: Resolve the hour as one unit rather than digit by digit: if both digits are hidden use 23; if only the tens is hidden pick 2 unless the units digit exceeds 3, in which case pick 1; if only the units is hidden pick 3 after a leading 2, otherwise 9. Minutes are independent: hidden tens becomes 5, hidden units becomes 9. Constant time and space.
s: If both hour digits are ?, write 23.
Else if the tens is ?, write 2 when the units digit is ? or ≤ 3, else 1.
Else if the units is ?, write 3 after a leading 2 and 9 otherwise.
Replace hidden minute tens with 5 and units with 9; return the repaired string.
a.t: O(1) — four character inspections regardless of input.
a.sp: O(1) — a small character buffer in immutable-string languages.

w: Lead with the joint greedy, but call out the trap explicitly — a pattern like "?4" must become 14, not an invalid 24 — because that interaction is the entire difficulty of the problem. Sanity-test at least "?:??", "?4:..", "2?:..", and fully visible times. The brute force is worth mentioning as a self-checking alternative and is genuinely preferable if you fear case-analysis bugs under interview pressure. Follow-ups: earliest valid time (mirror every choice), the number of valid times (multiply independent choices — see Number of Valid Clock Times), or adapting to a 12-hour clock.
